title: Builder's Preferred Lender in Myrtle Beach: Worth It?
description: Should you use the builder's preferred lender on a new home in Myrtle Beach? What the law says, how builder incentives work, and how to compare the whole loan.
h1: Should You Use the Builder's Preferred Lender? New Construction on the Grand Strand
dek: Buying a new home in Myrtle Beach? The builder's incentive is only half the story. Here's how to compare the whole loan.

faq.q: Can a builder make you use their lender?
faq.a: When a builder owns part of a lender, federal law allows it only if the builder doesn't require you to use that lender and gives you a written notice of the relationship. Any incentive for using it must be optional.

faq.q: Is the builder's preferred lender cheaper?
faq.a: Sometimes, but an incentive is only one number. Compare the interest rate, the lender fees and the cash to close on full Loan Estimates from the builder's lender and at least one other lender.

faq.q: Can I keep the builder incentive if I use my own lender?
faq.a: It depends on the builder. Many tie the incentive to their lender. Read the incentive terms in the contract, then compare what you'd save with each lender.

faq.q: How do I compare two mortgage offers?
faq.a: Ask each lender for a Loan Estimate. For most home loans, it must be sent within three business days of your application, and the standard form lets you compare the rate, fees and cash to close line by line.
